text: Replace pointwise BCE with within-user RankNet pairwise loss while retaining the current user, video, and request-context inputs, optimizer family, and canonical displayed-candidate evaluation.
rationale: The current scorer reaches GAUC 0.6689 and nDCG@5 0.5370, but its pointwise objective is not directly aligned with within-user ordering. Pairwise training is a focused objective ablation with plausible GAUC upside.
exact_ablation: Change only the training objective from row-wise BCE to within-user RankNet loss using positive-negative pairs from the same intact user candidate group; keep features, model capacity, optimizer, sampling limits, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive gain of +0.001 to +0.006 because the loss directly optimizes positive-over-negative ordering within users.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected flat to modestly positive change of -0.001 to +0.004; top-five gains depend on whether sampled pairs include high-scoring negatives.

text: Replace pointwise BCE with mixed-group ListNet top-one loss over intact within-user candidate groups, preserving the existing feature inputs and model scorer.
rationale: nDCG@5 is only 0.5370 despite respectable overall GAUC, motivating a listwise objective that explicitly concentrates probability mass near the top of each displayed group.
exact_ablation: Change only the loss from row-wise BCE to group-mean ListNet top-one cross-entropy on mixed-label groups, with fixed temperatures and no auxiliary BCE; retain the same inputs, architecture, optimizer, and group population.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected flat to modestly positive change of -0.001 to +0.004 because group normalization may improve local ordering but can discard absolute propensity information.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected modest positive gain of +0.001 to +0.008 because the objective emphasizes competition among candidates at the top of each group.

text: Use user-normalized pointwise BCE so each user contributes equal total training weight, while keeping the current additive model, request-context features, optimizer, and evaluation unchanged.
rationale: The objective is positive-count-weighted GAUC, while ordinary row-wise BCE can overrepresent users with many impressions. Equal user weighting is a low-complexity objective alternative that retains all-negative and all-positive groups.
exact_ablation: Change only the BCE reduction from unweighted row mean to exact inverse-user-candidate-count weighting computed from complete training groups; retain all rows, features, architecture, optimizer, and early-stopping rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive or flat change of 0.000 to +0.004 if long candidate lists currently dominate training; a small decline remains possible from noisier gradients.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected flat to small positive change of -0.002 to +0.003 because the loss remains pointwise and does not explicitly target the top five.

text: Keep the current pointwise BCE and scorer but train with group-complete, label-stratified minibatches so mixed, zero-positive, and all-positive user groups are sampled by group count.
rationale: The zero-positive validation slice contains 21,807 rows and has nDCG@5 of zero by definition, while the current random row minibatches may provide inconsistent exposure to useful mixed groups. This changes optimization exposure without changing labels or features.
exact_ablation: Change only minibatch construction to complete-group sampling with a fixed 60% mixed, 20% zero-positive, and 20% all-positive group mixture; retain pointwise BCE, features, model, optimizer hyperparameters, and number of optimization steps.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive gain of +0.0005 to +0.004 by supplying more stable within-user contrasts, with risk of decline if group reweighting mismatches the official population.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected flat to modestly positive change of -0.001 to +0.005 because mixed groups become more consistently represented during training.

text: Add a single multiplicative tab-by-hour interaction to the existing user/video/request-context scorer, leaving all original fields and training settings unchanged.
rationale: Request context was the only screened feature family with positive train-only primary lift (+0.00221), while official diagnostics show large variation by tab and hour. A targeted interaction tests whether context effects are non-additive rather than adding a broad static bundle.
exact_ablation: Add only one learned interaction feature representing the pair (tab, hour); retain the existing user, video, tab, hour, and weekday inputs, additive scorer, loss, optimizer, and training schedule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected modest positive gain of +0.001 to +0.005 because context-dependent candidate ordering may address heterogeneous tab and hour behavior.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected small positive or flat change of -0.001 to +0.004; interaction sparsity may limit top-five benefit.

text: Replace categorical hour with a compact cyclic hour representation while retaining tab, weekday, user, and video inputs and the same additive scorer and training procedure.
rationale: Several hour segments are weak, including hour 3 with GAUC 0.5318 and hour 4 with GAUC 0.6041. A cyclic representation shares statistical strength between adjacent hours without introducing any unavailable data.
exact_ablation: Replace only the categorical hour feature with two impression-time numeric features sin(2πhour/24) and cos(2πhour/24); keep tab, weekday, IDs, architecture, loss, optimizer, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected flat to modestly positive change of -0.001 to +0.003 by smoothing sparse hour estimates, though categorical effects that are non-smooth may be lost.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected flat to small positive change of -0.002 to +0.003 because the representation may improve generalization but does not directly emphasize top ranks.

text: Replace the additive scorer with a shallow cross network over the existing user, video, tab, hour, and weekday fields, testing explicit low-order feature interactions without adding new data sources.
rationale: The current additive model can only sum independent field effects. The positive request-context screen and severe tab-specific weaknesses suggest that user-item-context interactions may be more useful than additional first-order terms.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive linear scorer with a one-layer cross network plus linear output over the same five encoded fields; keep the input fields, loss, optimizer, training schedule, and evaluation fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive gain of +0.001 to +0.006 if context changes candidate ordering conditionally on user or video identity; overfitting could make it flat or negative.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected small positive gain of 0.000 to +0.005, with less confidence because added interactions may not focus on the highest-ranked errors.

text: Add a causally truncated recent-video history representation to the current scorer, using only prior events strictly before each impression and retaining the existing request-context inputs.
rationale: The official model has GAUC 0.6689 but weak top-five performance, leaving room for immediate-intent personalization. A bounded prior-history representation is a materially different feature family and can vary scores among the same user's candidate videos.
exact_ablation: Add only a bounded causal history feature consisting of the last 20 prior video IDs plus a missing-history indicator; emit features before updating state, and keep the existing additive scorer, loss, optimizer, and request-context fields unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected modest positive gain of +0.001 to +0.007 for users with repeatable preferences, with little effect for users lacking prior events.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected modest positive gain of +0.002 to +0.008 if recent intent identifies which candidates should occupy the top five; sparse-history cohorts may remain flat.

text: Replace the additive scorer with a candidate-conditioned attention module over a strictly causal recent-video history, while preserving the request-context fields and official displayed-candidate evaluation.
rationale: A fixed history representation can blur multiple interests. Candidate-conditioned attention could selectively activate different prior videos for different candidates, potentially improving both within-user ordering and top-five placement beyond first-order context effects.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive scorer with a candidate-conditioned attention scorer over the last 20 prior video IDs, using strict pre-impression cutoffs and masked attention; retain the same request-context fields, target, official split, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected positive but uncertain change of +0.001 to +0.008 when users have multiple relevant interests; cold or sparse-history users may regress.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected modest positive gain of +0.002 to +0.010 because candidate-relative history matching can promote the most relevant items into the top five.

text: Use a hybrid objective combining the existing pointwise BCE with a bounded within-user pairwise RankNet term, testing whether ranking alignment improves ordering without discarding row-level supervision.
rationale: The current model's respectable GAUC and lower nDCG@5 suggest a trade-off between preserving broad supervision and emphasizing ranking. A small pairwise auxiliary term is distinct from a full loss replacement and offers a safer fallback for homogeneous groups.
exact_ablation: Add only a RankNet pairwise loss weighted at 0.25 to the existing pointwise BCE, with pairs formed only within intact mixed user groups; retain the existing scorer, features, optimizer, and evaluation.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive gain of +0.001 to +0.005 because pairwise gradients target within-user ordering while BCE preserves broad supervision.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected flat to modestly positive change of -0.001 to +0.006; the auxiliary term may improve top ranks without destabilizing sparse groups.

text: Retain pointwise BCE but use a deterministic mixture of uniform and current-model hard-negative sampling within each user's displayed candidate group, without changing the scorer or feature set.
rationale: The current validation has GAUC 0.6689 but only 0.5370 nDCG@5, consistent with a need to focus training on confusing high-scoring negatives. Within-group hard-negative sampling remains compatible with the displayed-candidate task and avoids synthetic catalog negatives.
exact_ablation: Change only negative minibatch sampling to 50% uniform and 50% highest-current-score negatives within the same user's training candidate group, refreshed between epochs; retain pointwise BCE, features, architecture, optimizer, and total pair/example budget.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected modest positive gain of +0.001 to +0.005 by emphasizing difficult positive-negative orderings, with risk of overfitting repeated hard negatives.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected modest positive gain of +0.001 to +0.007 because high-scoring false positives receive more corrective updates.

text: Add a shallow nonlinear MLP over the existing encoded fields while keeping the same user, video, tab, hour, and weekday inputs, pointwise BCE, optimizer, and temporal split.
rationale: The additive model provides a strong low-cost reference but cannot represent nonlinear combinations among the positive request-context fields. This is a bounded architecture ablation rather than a broad static-feature expansion or capacity sweep.
exact_ablation: Replace only the additive score computation with a fixed two-layer MLP of widths 64 and 32 over the same five field embeddings; retain feature inputs, pointwise BCE, optimizer settings, training schedule, and evaluation unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Expected small positive or flat change of -0.002 to +0.005 because nonlinear interactions may repair context-specific ordering but may overfit sparse tab combinations.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Expected small positive gain of 0.000 to +0.005 if nonlinear interactions improve candidate separation near the top; a slight decline is possible from unstable score fitting.
